environment.description: Same Flask application deployed behind an nginx reverse proxy (v1.25.3) with a location block that appends response headers via add_header directive. The nginx configuration includes 'add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ws://$host wss://$host; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'" always;' applied to all proxied responses including WebSocket upgrade responses. Note: the 'always' parameter ensures the header is added even on error responses. The nginx proxy_pass forwards to the Flask backend on localhost:5000. Additionally, the nginx config sets 'proxy_hide_header X-Powered-By' and 'add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff always'. The CSP does NOT include 'unsafe-inline' in the script-src directive, meaning any injected inline script tags or event handlers delivered via WebSocket messages that get inserted into the DOM via innerHTML will be blocked by the browser's CSP enforcement engine before execution.

config.nginx_location_block: location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:5000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_set_header Host $host; add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ws://$host wss://$host; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'" always; add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff always; proxy_hide_header X-Powered-By; }
config.network: nginx listens on 443 with TLS, Flask bound to localhost only
